subject: Polity
description: PAC, Estimates Committee, Public Undertakings Committee, DRSCs, Business Advisory Committee

questions.stem: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) of Indian Parliament has how many members at present?

options.option_text: 22 — 15 from Lok Sabha + 7 from Rajya Sabha

questions.explanation: PAC — total 22 members (15 LS + 7 RS) elected for 1 year. Tradition since 1967: Chair from the Opposition (a courtesy, not constitutional). Set up first in 1921 under Government of India Act 1919. Examines Audit Reports of CAG laid before Parliament — finds whether public money was spent for the authorised purpose. PAC cannot question policy; only review accounts. Often called the 'twin' of Estimates Committee + Committee on Public Undertakings.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Estimates Committee — the largest financial committee in Parliament — consists of:

options.option_text: 30 members all from Lok Sabha (no Rajya Sabha members)

questions.explanation: Estimates Committee — 30 members ALL from Lok Sabha (no Rajya Sabha representation). Originally 25 (1950), increased to 30 in 1956. Constituted annually. Sometimes called 'Continuous Economy Committee' — examines budget estimates of ministries and suggests economies. Cannot examine matters relating to the Defence Department's secret operations. Chair is appointed by Speaker from among members. PAC and Estimates Committee together oversee 'before' and 'after' aspects of public expenditure.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Departmentally Related Standing Committees (DRSCs) were established in 1993 (initially 17, now 24). Each committee has:
questions.explanation: DRSCs — 24 standing committees, each with 31 members (21 LS + 10 RS), 1-year term. Each examines bills + budget demands + annual reports of one or more allied ministries. Chair drawn from majority OR opposition (rotates). Major reform in legislative scrutiny — ministers can't be members. 8 DRSCs serviced by Rajya Sabha Secretariat (chaired by RS members), 16 by Lok Sabha Secretariat. Bills are referred for clause-by-clause examination before passage.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 'Business Advisory Committee' (BAC) of Lok Sabha is chaired by:
questions.explanation: Business Advisory Committee — 15 members in Lok Sabha (chaired by Speaker), 11 in Rajya Sabha (chaired by Chairman). Recommends time allocation for legislative and other business. Effectively decides the parliamentary calendar. The Speaker / Chairman is the binding authority — committee functions advisorily. Decisions usually reached by consensus among parties' representatives. Other key Lok Sabha committees: Rules Committee (chaired by Speaker), Committee on Privileges, Ethics Committee, Committee on Government Assurances.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a financial committee of Indian Parliament?
questions.explanation: Three financial committees: PAC (22 members — 15 LS + 7 RS), Estimates Committee (30, LS only), Committee on Public Undertakings (22 — 15 LS + 7 RS, examines reports of PSUs). Committee on Subordinate Legislation is a SCRUTINY committee (15 LS members) — examines whether powers to make rules/regulations conferred by Parliament are being properly exercised. Other scrutiny committees: Committee on Government Assurances, Committee on Petitions.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which kind of parliamentary committee is constituted to examine a particular bill / matter and ceases to exist on submission of its report?

options.option_text: Ad-hoc Committee (e.g. Select Committee, Joint Parliamentary Committee)

questions.explanation: Ad-hoc committees — formed for a specific purpose, dissolve on report submission. Sub-types: Select Committee (one House), Joint Committee (both Houses), JPC (Joint Parliamentary Committee — has investigative powers, e.g. JPC on Bofors 1987, 2G 2011, NRC). Standing committees are permanent / annually reconstituted (PAC, Estimates, CoPU, DRSCs, BAC). 'Committee of the Whole House' = the entire House sitting as a committee, usually for the Finance Bill or Appropriation Bill clause-by-clause discussion.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Tradition since 1967: the Chairmanship of the Public Accounts Committee is given to:

options.option_text: The senior-most member of the ruling party
A member from the Opposition (usually the Leader of the Opposition or a senior Opposition MP)

questions.explanation: Convention since 1967 — PAC Chair from the Opposition, ensuring independence in scrutinising government accounts. The chair is appointed by the Speaker. This is a CONVENTION (not constitutional / statutory) — the only similar convention is for the Estimates Committee NOT to be chaired by an Opposition member (it remains with the ruling side). The first PAC Chairman was K.M. Munshi (1949-50), 1st Opposition PAC Chair was M.R. Masani (1967-69).
